vocabulary.meaning_en: to teach someone how to do a job
vocabulary.example: Anna will show Denise the ropes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to begin working on something
vocabulary.example: Why don't you make a start on this report?

vocabulary.meaning_en: for some time
vocabulary.example: Just watch what I do for a while.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to train and help someone improve
vocabulary.example: She is coaching the new staff.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make someone feel less worried
vocabulary.example: He reassured me that the job was easy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person whose job is to sell a company's products
vocabulary.example: Denise is training to be a Sales Executive.

vocabulary.meaning_en: knowledge and skill you get from doing something
vocabulary.example: She wanted some experience in sales.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having skill from doing something many times
vocabulary.example: He's an experienced manager.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large set of information stored on a computer
vocabulary.example: Check the database for the customer's number.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a piece of work you have to do
vocabulary.example: My first task is to check emails.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the rules or terms of an agreement or job
vocabulary.example: She negotiated new conditions with her boss.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to discuss to reach an agreement
vocabulary.example: She negotiated a better salary.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to admit that what you said was wrong
vocabulary.example: He said it would fail, but he had to eat his words.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to continue to live or exist through a difficult time
vocabulary.example: We couldn't survive without you!

vocabulary.meaning_en: to go away so someone can do their work
vocabulary.example: I'll leave you to it.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a phone call not about work
vocabulary.example: Please don't make personal calls at work.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the way you speak on the phone
vocabulary.example: She has a very polite phone manner.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to ask a company to send you goods
vocabulary.example: Could you order some pens?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to have none left
vocabulary.example: We've run out of pens.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person you work with
vocabulary.example: My colleagues are very helpful.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a new job or position
vocabulary.example: How are you finding your new role?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to become comfortable in a new place or job
vocabulary.example: It takes a few weeks to settle in.

fine_lines.title: experience vs experiment
fine_lines.explanation_ar: experience خبرة أو تجربة عشتها. experiment تجربة علمية لاختبار شيء ما. يخلط بينهما العرب لأن كلمة «تجربة» تترجم الاثنتين.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Experience = knowledge from doing things. Experiment = a scientific test.

examples.sentence: She has five years' experience in sales.
The students did an experiment in the lab.

fine_lines.title: make a start vs start
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى متقارب، لكن make a start on أسلوب ألطف ويُستخدم كثيرًا في الإنجليزية البريطانية لتشجيع شخص على البدء في مهمة: Why don't you make a start on this?
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean begin. 'Make a start on' sounds softer and is common in British English for encouraging someone.

examples.sentence: Why don't you make a start on these emails?

expressions.phrase: Let me show you the ropes.
expressions.meaning_en: I'll teach you how to do this job.
expressions.example: Welcome to the team! Let me show you the ropes.

expressions.phrase: Watch what I do for a while.
expressions.meaning_en: Look at how I work first.
expressions.example: Don't answer the phone yet. Watch what I do for a while.

expressions.phrase: Why don't you make a start on this?
expressions.meaning_ar: لماذا لا تبدأ في هذه المهمة؟
expressions.meaning_en: A friendly way to give someone a task.
expressions.example: Why don't you make a start on the customer list?

expressions.phrase: I'm here to help, so please ask me if you need to know what to do.
expressions.meaning_ar: أنا هنا للمساعدة، فاسألني من فضلك إن احتجت إلى معرفة ما يجب فعله.
expressions.example: I'm here to help, so please ask me if you need anything.
Nice to have you back after your holiday!

expressions.phrase: We just couldn't survive without you.
expressions.meaning_ar: لم نكن نستطيع الاستمرار من دونك.
expressions.meaning_en: You are very important to us (friendly exaggeration).
expressions.example: Welcome back! We just couldn't survive without you.

expressions.meaning_en: I'll go so you can continue.
expressions.example: You know what to do now, so I'll leave you to it.

grammar.title: Why don't you + verb? (suggestion)
grammar.explanation_ar: Why don't you + الفعل الأساسي؟ ليس سؤالًا حقيقيًا عن السبب، بل اقتراح أو طلب لطيف.
grammar.explanation_en: 'Why don't you + base verb?' is a friendly suggestion or instruction, not a real question.
examples: Why don't you make a start on this?
Why don't you call the client?
Why don't you take a break?

grammar.title: Imperatives for instructions + let me
grammar.explanation_ar: عند تعليم شخص نستخدم الأمر بصيغة الفعل الأساسي (Watch, Check) و Let me + فعل لعرض أنك ستفعل شيئًا: Let me show you.
grammar.explanation_en: Use imperatives (Watch, Check) to give instructions and 'Let me + verb' to offer to do something.
examples: Let me show you the ropes.
Watch what I do for a while.

grammar.title: if + need to know
grammar.explanation_ar: please ask me if you need to know what to do: بعد if نستخدم المضارع البسيط، وبعد know يمكن أن نضع what to do / how to do it.
grammar.explanation_en: Use if + present simple; after 'know' use what/how + to + verb.
examples: Please ask me if you need to know what to do.
Tell me if you don't know how to use it.
Ask Tom if you need to know where to go.

questions.question: 'Show someone the ropes' means ___.
choices: teach someone how to do a job
questions.explanation_en: It means teach someone the job.

questions.question: Why don't you ___ a start on this?
questions.explanation_en: The phrase is 'make a start on'.

questions.question: Watch what I do ___ a while.
'Why don't you make a start on this?' is ___.
Anna asks Denise to check the ___ to see which clients haven't been called.
Denise wants ___ in sales.
questions.explanation_en: Experience means skill from doing something.

questions.question: I'm here to help, so please ask me if you ___ to know what to do.
Paul said Denise had to go, but then asked her back. He had to ___.
questions.explanation_en: It means admit you were wrong.

questions.question: 'I'll leave you to it' means ___.
choices: I'll go so you can do your work
questions.explanation_en: I'll go so you can continue.

questions.question: To make someone feel less worried is to ___ them.
